- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, reduce forecast for next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot; model should show mean reversion toward prior 10-day average.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.4), adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s recent direction, not just historical trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, reweight forecast toward recent 7-day average to reduce lag.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.35, -0.40), model should anticipate downward correction and reduce forecast slope.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates early in 30-day window (e.g., first 7 days), apply downward bias of 3–5% to correct for momentum overcorrection.
